citation: Oberoi A, Giezenaar C, Rigda RS, et al. Comparative Effects of Co-Ingesting Whey Protein and Glucose Alone and Combined on Blood Glucose, Plasma Insulin and Glucagon Concentrations in Younger and Older Men. Nutrients. 2022;14(15):3111.
protocol: Drinks after an overnight fast: control (~2 kcal), 30 g whey protein (120 kcal), 30 g glucose (120 kcal), 30 g whey + 30 g glucose (240 kcal); crossover; buffet meal at 180 min. Blood at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 min.
population: 10 healthy younger men (18-35 y, 29 ± 2 y, BMI 26.1 ± 0.4) and 10 healthy older men (68-87 y, 78 ± 2 y); Australia (Adelaide).

reports.where: Table 1: fasting, peak, time to peak, return to baseline, net iAUC 0-60 and 0-180 per drink and age group

note: Separates protein alone, glucose alone and both together, in young and old men, with glucagon. Insulin is in mU/L. It is a drink rather than a food meal, but the protein-only arm is exactly what the model lacks. Only in figures: time courses. Meal kinds: protein load, liquid meal.
